feature.summary: Rules for what memory may hold and use. People list terms to never remember; credentials and other prohibited facts are refused for every source; sensitive topics need opt-in for automatic saves. Temporary chats neither read nor save memory. Web and mobile show which memories a reply used. The server applies one memory context to every model.

purpose.what_it_does: Enforces privacy rules on memory: a never-remember list of terms, automatic refusal of credential-like and other prohibited facts, an opt-in for sensitive topics, temporary chats that skip memory completely, a 'Memory · N' indication on replies that used memory, and the same memory for every model and every signed-in client.
purpose.why_it_exists: People must be able to stop sensitive information being remembered and see when memory shaped a reply. Brief S39.27 to S39.32 and docs/product/requirements.md:765 require temporary chats to neither update nor reference memory.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who uses memory; privacy-minded people; workspace admins relying on policy; testers.
problems_solved: Passwords, payment details or identifiers ending up in memory.
Private topics being remembered without consent.
Not knowing whether an answer came from memory.
Memory working on one model or app and not another.
use_cases: Add 'home address' to Never remember; a later attempt to save a fact containing it is refused with a message naming the term.
Start a temporary chat and tell the assistant a fact; it is not saved and no memory is read.
Open a reply's 'Memory · 3' control to see which saved facts were used.
Save a fact in the CLI and see it on web and in VS Code.

journey: 1. Open Settings, Memory, Never remember and add a term.
2. Any later save (typed, imported, auto-saved or spoken 'remember') whose text contains the term is refused.
3. Credentials and other prohibited facts are refused with a reason for every source.
4. Start a temporary chat: memory is neither read nor saved.
5. In a normal chat, if memory shaped a reply, open Memory · N to see which facts.
6. Pick any model; the same memory is used.
feedback_and_outputs: Refusal text: 'Not saved. This memory contains "<term>", which you asked AGI never to remember.' (apps/web/lib/services/memory-write-service.ts:24).
Sensitive-topic refusal explaining Remember that ... or the opt-in switch (packages/contracts/context/src/memory-content-policy.ts:580).
Temporary chat reply: 'This is a temporary chat, so it neither reads nor saves Memory.' (apps/web/lib/server/tools/memory-tools.ts:121).
Banner text on mobile: 'Won't appear in history or use memory, and is normally deleted after 30 days.' (Cloud) and a Local version (TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:12-15).
CLI: 'Not remembered: <reason>' and import counts of excluded items.
settings: Never remember list and source suppression (user settings memory namespace).

working: Exclusions are stored in user settings (memory.excludedTerms), normalized to lower case, at least 3 characters, at most 50 (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:283-300).

Typed saves, edits, sync pushes, imports, explicit remember commands and automatic saves all check the list; a read failure refuses the write (apps/web/lib/services/memory-write-service.ts:39,44; apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:148; apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:170; apps/web/app/api/memory/import/route.ts:107; apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:114; managed-memory-context-service.ts:1372).

Prohibited categories are credential, payment_instrument, government_identifier, biometric, precise_location, criminal_history and immigration_status, and are refused for every source (packages/contracts/context/src/memory-content-policy.ts:1-9; managed-memory-context-service.ts:570).

Sensitive topics (health, ethnic origin, religion, politics, sexual orientation, gender identity, union membership) are refused for automatic saves unless the person opts in or explicitly asks (memory-content-policy.ts:13-21; managed-memory-context-service.ts:603-640).

A temporary conversation gets a disabled memory policy and no memory or past-chat read; past-chat search excludes temporary chats (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:4126; apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts:124-131; apps/web/lib/services/past-chat-context-service.ts:256). Memory tools refuse in temporary chats (memory-tools.ts:121).
A temporary chat may still ask to forget, never to remember (memory-commands.ts:71).

Server sends memory citations with the reply; web shows 'Memory · N' and mobile a 'Memory · N' chip (request-processor.ts:6889; ResearchPanel.tsx:156; MemoryUsedChip.tsx:13; chatExecutionStore.ts:3459).

Memory is loaded by user, workspace, project and source filters only, with no model input, so every model gets the same context (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1128). Local-model turns on web and desktop prefetch the same account context (apps/web/app/api/memory/local-context/route.ts; apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:4479).

Memory crosses clients through /api/memory and /api/memory/sync (apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:393; apps/cli/src/cloud/memory.rs:15; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/memoryClient.ts:43; apps/extension-vscode/src/memory/accountMemoryClient.ts).
Mobile temporary chat reads no memory and skips memory commands and capture (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2797,2962).
incomplete: Never-remember is account-level: mobile Local writes check credentials and sensitive topics but not the term list (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/localMemoryWriter.ts:25-35; excludedTerms appears only in memory-exclusions.tsx).

Temporary chat in CLI, VS Code and Chrome: CLI offers --no-memory and --no-session-persistence flags (lib.rs:6691) but no temporary chat; Chrome has a temporary chat mode whose server-side memory effect depends on the server marking the conversation temporary [inferred from request-processor.ts:4081,4126; side_panel.ts:1095]; VS Code none found.
The brief lists the memory-used indication as missing on mobile, but mobile has it (MemoryUsedChip.tsx); CLI, VS Code, Chrome and desktop Tauri have none found.

Mobile temporary chat 'Personalized' option sets personalization true or false; the server turns memory off when personalization is false (request-processor.ts:3523), and what 'Personalized' adds in a temporary chat beyond instructions is not traced.
disconnected_or_disabled: Model-based extraction of automatic memories is switched by the environment setting AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION and only runs when the turn text was kept (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:36-58; docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:53-58).

established.statement: The user can stop sensitive information being remembered (never-remember terms or categories) and sensitive facts such as credentials are refused automatically.
In a temporary chat nothing is read from or saved to memory, and the chat is never used later as past-chat context.
When saved memory or past chats shaped a reply, the reply shows it and which memories.
Saved memory and personalization apply the same way whichever model the user picks.
A memory saved on one client appears and is used on every other client signed in to the same account.
Temporary chats must not update or reference memory unless the user explicitly changes that behavior.
Mobile keeps Local and Cloud memory separate; one is never copied into the other.
Temporary chats, Memory-off sessions, API and zero-data-retention traffic stay excluded from automatic extraction.

acceptance_criteria: Adding 'home address' to Never remember then saving 'my home address is X' by typing, import, remember command and auto-save all refuse with the term named.
A fact that looks like a password or card number is refused in every app that writes memory.
A health-related fact is not auto-saved unless 'Include sensitive topics in memory' is on; saying 'Remember that ...' saves it.
In a temporary chat on web and mobile, no memory is read, no fact is saved, and the chat is not found by past-chat search.
A normal reply that used memory shows 'Memory · N' listing the facts on web and mobile.
The same prompt on two different models gets the same memory context.
A fact added in the CLI shows in web Settings, Memory and in VS Code after sync.
Exclusion terms shorter than 3 characters are rejected with a message.
inferred: Never-remember should also apply to mobile Local memory to meet 'stop sensitive info being remembered' there [inferred from the account-level list and the local writer].
The Chrome temporary chat probably excludes memory through the server's temporary conversation check [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Apply the term list in the mobile Local writer using a device copy of the list.
[proposed] Show the memory-used indication in the CLI and in VS Code chat.
[proposed] Add a never-remember screen to desktop Tauri and Chrome.

steps.what_happens: Person adds a term; the client saves it in the account's memory settings namespace.
Any memory write reaches the server, which loads the list (failing closed on error), then runs the content and policy gate.
For a chat turn the server checks if the conversation is temporary; if so it uses a disabled memory policy and loads no memory or past chats.
Otherwise it loads memories filtered by user, workspace, project and suppressed sources, ranks them against the question, takes up to 30, and places them in the prompt fenced as untrusted data.
The model provider receives the prompt; the reply stream carries memory citations back to the app.
The app shows 'Memory · N' from the citations.
After the turn, automatic saving extracts facts, applies the exclusions and the eligibility gate and writes rows.
Other clients pull the new rows by delta sync.

data.synced: Read by every client of the account
data.retained_or_deleted: Until the person removes them; existing memories containing a term are not deleted (MemoryExclusions.tsx:162 copy)

data.where_stored: table user_memories; citations travel in the reply metadata and are stored on the assistant message
data.retained_or_deleted: Deleted memories keep a text-less tombstone (managed-memory-context-service.ts:391)
Purged by a scheduled job; mobile banner says normally deleted after 30 days (purge-temporary-chats/route.ts:30; TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:12)
Cleared by the person or by data deletion (apps/mobile/services/dsarExport.ts)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Memory is added by the server for every model and provider and no model identifier enters the query (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1128). Auto-extraction may use a utility model route when the environment flag is on and the turn is not zero-data-retention (managed-auto-memory-service.ts:36-58). On Local-model turns on web and desktop the device asks for account memory and injects it itself (useChatStream.ts:4479); in own-key and Local modes content outside Managed storage is never saved to user_memories (trust_mode_outside_managed_storage, managed-memory-context-service.ts:540,654).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account for the term list and for Cloud memory. Mobile Local memory needs none.
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace policy can close memory entirely (managed-memory-context-service.ts:115). The person controls their own switches.
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code for these rules.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: 50 terms of 3 to 100 characters; 30 memories and 8,000 characters per prompt; at most 5 automatic memories per turn (managed-memory-context-service.ts:67,71,72 MAX_AUTO_MEMORIES_PER_TURN); mobile reads 5 facts per local turn (chatExecutionStore.ts retrieveMemoryContext(content, 5)).
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION for model-based auto extraction; user switches memory, generateFromHistory, searchPastChats, includeSensitiveTopics, allowToolAssistedGeneration (readUserMemoryCapabilities, managed-memory-context-service.ts:258).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Same for every model; no capability check was found. Tool-assisted memory generation has its own switch.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Memory is not saved from turns in own-key or Local trust modes (managed-memory-context-service.ts:654). Content tied to Google user data is excluded from memory reads (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1170 memoryFreeOfGoogleUserDataSql).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Mobile Local mode keeps memory on the device, refuses credentials and sensitive topics, skips memory in temporary chats, and has no never-remember term check (localMemoryWriter.ts:25-35). CLI Local sessions do not receive account memory; only Managed sessions do (apps/cli/src/cloud/memory.rs header).

corrections.claim: Limits: 50 terms of 3 to 100 characters; 30 memories and 8,000 characters per prompt; at most 5 automatic memories per turn; mobile reads 5 facts per local turn
corrections.what_the_code_shows: MAX_MEMORIES=30, MAX_TOTAL_MEMORY_CHARS=8000 and MAX_AUTO_MEMORIES_PER_TURN=5 are right (lines 67-72). The 50 and 3 limits are right. The 100-character limit exists only as maxLength={100} on the web input; the server normalizer sets no maximum length. Mobile retrieveMemoryContext(content, 5) is right, but it runs only when memory reads are enabled and !serverAssemblesContext. In Cloud mode the server builds the context instead.
corrections.correction: Terms must be at least 3 characters, with at most 50 per account. The 100-character cap is a web input limit only and the server does not enforce it. Mobile reads up to 5 local facts per turn only when the app, not the server, assembles the context.

corrections.claim: Local mode: mobile Local refuses credentials and sensitive topics and has no never-remember term check; CLI Local sessions get no account memory, only Managed ones
corrections.what_the_code_shows: localMemoryWriter always refuses prohibited categories. It refuses sensitive topics only when source==='learned' and includeSensitiveTopics!==true, so explicit saves of sensitive topics go through. It has no term check, and excludedTerms is used only in memory-exclusions.tsx. The CLI header says only a Managed session's prompt carries account memory, which is right.
corrections.correction: Mobile Local refuses credential-like and other prohibited facts for every source. It refuses sensitive topics only for learned (automatic) saves unless the person opted in. It does not check the never-remember list.

corrections.claim: Desktop Tauri: no never-remember list found; temporary-chat coverage lists only web, mobile and Chrome
corrections.what_the_code_shows: No exclusion UI exists in apps/desktop/src. Desktop does have a Local-mode temporary chat: useTemporaryChatControl creates an incognito conversation that is never written to SQLite, and its comment says the native runtime skips memory for it. The page never mentions it, and acceptance criterion 4 covers only web and mobile. A Memory settings tab also exists (features/settings/tabs/Memory.tsx) and is not described.
corrections.correction: Add: desktop Tauri has a Local-mode temporary chat (incognito conversation, not stored, memory skipped by the native runtime, switch works only on an empty chat). It has no never-remember list.

corrections.claim: Temporary chats are purged by a scheduled job; mobile banner says normally deleted after 30 days (purge-temporary-chats/route.ts:30; TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:12)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The banner text is right (TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:11-12). In the purge route, RETENTION_DAYS = 30 is at line 24, and line 30 is the GET handler's start. The queries I read (lines 45, 98, 105) filter candidate and job tables by created_at. I did not trace a delete of web_conversations with is_temporary, so the purge claim is not confirmed by the lines read.
corrections.correction: Cite route.ts:24 for the 30-day RETENTION_DAYS constant, and confirm that the job deletes web_conversations rows with is_temporary before stating it.

missing_facts: Mobile Personalized or Unpersonalized in a temporary chat: the page lists it as not traced. A request with personalization === false forces memory_enabled = false (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:3523). The mobile store sends personalization from temporaryChatPersonalized (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:3453,5216). The banner says Unpersonalized also leaves out profile, instructions and response style (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/TemporaryChatBanner.tsx:19-20).

Desktop Tauri has a Local-mode temporary chat (apps/desktop/src/features/chat/useTemporaryChat.ts:1-15) and a Memory settings tab (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/tabs/Memory.tsx). The page describes neither.

The server-side never-remember term check has no length cap. The 100-character limit exists only on the web input (apps/web/features/settings/components/MemoryExclusions.tsx:186). normalizeMemoryExclusions (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:289-298) enforces only the 3-character minimum and the 50-term maximum, so the CLI and VS Code can write longer terms.
